propositions: A single pending entry in the queue disables the O(1) fast-path gate marker store-wide, forcing full directory scans on every subsequent write.
The gate marker is written only when a full scan finds nothing pending, creating binary (all-or-nothing) behavior that costs O(store size) per write with any pending backlog.
The proposed live-set marker generalization scopes the walk to only tickets with active queue entries, reducing scoped-probe cost from O(store) to O(backlog) while preserving the O(1) quiet path.

The TTL-bounded marker is redesigned to always write on full scans (adding a 'live' field of ticket ids), with scoped probes never refreshing written_ns so the TTL still measures time since the last full walk.
New-enqueue operations continue to clear the marker immediately, and wrong-typed 'live' fields cause the entire marker to be distrusted and fall back to full scans.
The scan-helper extracting the f400 service-order sort ensures scoped and full-walk paths return identical ordering and pending verdicts for the same store state.
